newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's YPF says closes 59 oil wells due spill.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's YPF says closes 59 oil wells due spill.

text.p: Argentina's oil giant YPF SA said Wednesday it closed 59 wells due to a spill in its Rincon de los Sauces field in Patagonia, a move which affected three percent of the area's production.
The announcement was made soon after official sources said the government was ordering YPF to close 90 wells.
A company official told Reuters YPF had made the decision on its own and had so far received no communication from the government.
YPF said in a press release repair work was already under way and the pipeline should be fixed within the next 60 days.

The spillage into the Colorado River, which crosses five provinces from the Andes to the Atlantic, affected the town of Rincn de los Sauces -- in Neuquen province some 1,300 km (850 miles) south west of Buenos Aires -- which takes its drinking water from the Colorado.

YPF said Tuesday it will dig water wells to restore supplies to Rincon de los Sauces. Media reports said as many as 300,000 liters of crude may have seeped into the river upstream, where the oil wells are located, after recent storms.
YPF, which has a total of 1,500 wells and quotes in Wall Street, said the 59 wells capped represented a temporary loss of only 670 cubic meters per day.
It and other oil firms responsible for the crude leakages have said they will continue to provide local residents, schools and hospitals with mineral water until the problem is solved.
On Monday, the federal government signed a pact with the five provinces involved to ensure proper monitoring of oil firms after the damage to ducts.
The companies claimed that before the leaks on February 15 and March 6 and 7 they had hired international consultants to carry out a risk study which did not show any major threat.

YPF, Perez Companc, Petrolera San Jorge, Mexpetrol and Oldeval said in ads published in local newspapers last week that the leaks were caused by torrential rains and slides of water and rocks "which are completely abnormal in the area."
